---
# Surface Codes — Briefing

Surface codes are a family of 2D topological quantum error-correcting codes [1]. They require only nearest-neighbor 2D connectivity, making them hardware-friendly [1]. The threshold is approximately 1% for circuit-level noise [1].

The stabilizer formalism provides a group-theoretic description [2]. The threshold theorem establishes that below threshold, logical error rates suppress exponentially with code distance [2].

Recent work has extended these ideas to biased-noise regimes [3], though the exact threshold behavior remains an open question.

## References

[1] Surface codes: Towards practical large-scale quantum computation
[2] Quantum Computation and Quantum Information — Chapter 10

# Stabilizer Formalism

> The group-theoretic framework underlying most stabilizer QEC codes.

## Key points

USER HAND-EDITED THIS SECTION: I rewrote this to include my own understanding connecting it to the normalizer of the Pauli group. Below is my own prose, NOT the original capture output.

The stabilizer formalism describes codes as +1 eigenspaces of an abelian subgroup S of the Pauli group, where -I is not in S. The logical operators are elements of N(S)/S where N(S) is the normalizer of S.
